ops.expect: Late July through mid-September gives the most reliable snow-free scrambling on the upper mountain and summit ridge; snow, moats, and cornices can linger into July on the shadier saddle and upper gullies. Some parties instead climb it in late May-June as a steep snow route while the approach brush is still snow-covered, and it has been climbed in winter during stable high-pressure windows by strong, experienced parties.
ops.value: Late spring is the easiest time: snow still covers much of the brush and snowmelt gives water on the way up. The route faces south almost the whole way, so mid-summer is very hot, and by late summer and fall the lack of water makes it an ordeal. It has also been climbed in winter during stable spells by strong, experienced parties.

expect.optimalWindow: Mid-July through September, once approach snow has melted out;

July.reason: Approach snow is often still lingering in shaded gullies and on the upper mountain early in the month; brushy lower approach can still be wet

August.reason: Most reliable window - approach typically fully melted out, driest rock, most stable access along the highway corridor

September.reason: Stable early in the month with continued dry rock; increasing chance of early-season snow and shortening daylight later in the month

value.optimalWindow: Late spring, while snow still covers the brush and snowmelt provides water

May.reason: Snow still suppresses the brush and snowmelt gives water on the south-facing slopes

July.reason: Mid-summer heat on an almost entirely south-facing route, with the brush fully exposed

August.reason: Hot and increasingly short of water on the way up

September.reason: Late-season lack of water can make the long climb an ordeal
